summary: Consult: rate-window and quota split for mixed low-latency chat + bulk embedding pipeline
description: Issue summary: Customer runs a mixed workload in a dedicated pool: low-latency chat (sub-200ms SLO) interleaved with large bulk embedding backfills. After a recent change to their batching client, they see frequent 429s on chat routes during concurrent backfills. Impact: chat latency degrades as client-side retries amplify throttles; customer reports significant UX regressions on production traffic. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated tier) backed by a 4-GPU nodeset, multiple routes defined (chat-priority, embeddings-bulk).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start continuous low-latency chat streamers at steady rate (~40 concurrent sessions).
2) Kick off a bulk embedding backfill (10k documents) from the same tenant using parallel workers (20 workers), each using batched /embeddings endpoint,
3) Observe token-level 429s reported on chat route within 2-5 minutes, and increased client-side retry waves.
4) Check rate-limit headers on chat responses and monitoring dashboards (per-route token-window exhaustion).

comments: 2026-03-10 14:15 - Aisha Rahman (support): Customer says this started after they upgraded their embedding uploader to aggressive parallelism and switched to larger batch sizes. They want guidance to avoid 429s for chat while maintaining bulk throughput.

2026-03-10 15:02 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Initial triage — looks like token-window exhaustion at the route layer. Possible causes: shared tenant token accounting between routes, burst credits being consumed by embeddings workers, and refill smoothing lag after refill. Pulling relevant metrics now.

2026-03-10 16:10 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Found correlated spikes in embeddings token consumption and a sawtooth pattern on the tenant-level refill. Slack thread: #support -> https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C05RATE/xyZ12345
2026-03-11 09:08 - Customer (AtlasSearch): Can we get a config recommendation? We need chat preserved at 200ms p95 and still finish the 10k job within 2 hours if possible.

2026-03-11 10:30 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Suggested workaround posted in console and sent via email: 1) create route-level quota separation for chat vs embeddings, 2) apply small priority weights giving chat higher priority, 3) schedule bulk with jitter and reduce parallel workers from 20 -> 6. Customer will test tonight.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Customer (AtlasSearch): After reducing workers to 6 and applying route quota split, chat 429s dropped ~95% and p95 latency returned to expected. Bulk runtime increased but remained within acceptable window. They asked for permanent config guidance and whether we can automate fallback to a cheaper embedding variant when bulk consumes burst credits.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Tenant-level token bucket was being depleted by synchronous accounting for bulk jobs — route-layer separation not enforced for their configuration.
Hypothesis B: Refill smoothing lag (refill_delay_ms spikes) allowed a transient drain that coincided with large multi-worker batch commits, creating retry waves that caused amplification.

Partial finding: Metrics show embeddings-bulk consumed ~85% of tenant tokens in busy windows; chat-priority had no dedicated per-route guarantee. Console snapshot: tenant_quota_utilization peaked at 98% during bulk high concurrency.
Related observability: trace ids and dashboards attached. Related internal doc: CON-ops-rate-windowing (https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Rate+Window+Behavior)
resolution: Workaround and immediate remediation: 1) We recommended splitting tenant quota into two route-level quotas (chat-priority: 40% guaranteed, embeddings-bulk: 60% with burst cap). 2) Set chat route priority class to 'latency-critical' which gives it preferential scheduling and an emergency reservation for small bursts. 3) Add client recommendations: reduce embedding parallelism, add exponential jitter on workers, and enable streaming embedding chunking to smooth token consumption. Outcome: customer reports immediate improvement after applying these changes. Longer-term action: create a console template 'dedicated-mixed-workload' to automatically suggest quota splits and gutter policies, and file an internal task to evaluate automatic fallback to quantized embedding model when tenant burst usage exceeds threshold.
